rules.title: Session cookie without Secure flag

negative.source: res.cookie('session', token, { secure: true, httpOnly: true });

adversarial.rationale: Identifier options are unverifiable at line level, so the rule stays visible until configuration is proven; review-first matches sibling cookie rules.

adversarial.source: res.cookie('session', token, { secure: false, httpOnly: true });
adversarial.rationale: Explicit secure:false is worse than omission; the negative lookahead treats any non-true occurrence as missing transport protection.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Any Secure occurrence suppresses the finding including explicit false, documented intentionally as review-first behavior. Non-session cookie names avoid the sensitive hints entirely.

rules.title: XXE protection explicitly disabled in Java parser

adversarial.rationale: Feature configuration hides behind a helper comment; line-level rules cannot verify helper bodies, matching the documented boundary.
Setting external-parameter-entities to FALSE is the protective direction; the rule fires only when protection features are explicitly disabled.

rules.false_positive_analysis: True-valued feature calls and bare newInstance() lines cannot match. The pattern requires a known XXE-protection feature id followed by an explicit false, making every hit a deliberate disablement.

rules.title: Ruby dynamic method invocation from request

negative.source: case params[:action] when 'publish' then publish end

adversarial.rationale: fetch() against a frozen action map is sanctioned allowlist indirection; the argument is a lookup result rather than params directly after send's open paren.
to_sym still yields an attacker-chosen method name; casting does not constrain the dispatch target and must remain flagged.

rules.false_positive_analysis: public_send with literal symbols, case-dispatch allowlists, and eval usage (covered separately) never match the params-directly-after-send shape. Fetch-map indirection documents the safe pattern the remediation recommends.

rules.title: Go command built by concatenation

adversarial.rationale: Slice-expansion of programmatically built args has no concatenation operator on the line; argv-boundary safety lives in buildArgs review.
Joining parts into one sh -c string reconstructs the shell-interpreter surface; helper indirection does not remove injection capability.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Fixed argv slices, variadic expansions of programmatic slices, and Context variants without concatenation stay silent. Any +-identifier token inside the call parentheses indicates assembled command text worth reviewing.

rules.false_positive_analysis: Only the literal colon-true struct field matches. False values, omitted fields, and commented samples stay silent. Assignment-form bypasses are intentionally surfaced as review-first.
